messages:
Maya: Heads up — this morning we hit sustained queuing on the shared-gpu pool in eu-west-1. Latency SLOs for small-req tenants spiked.
Samir: saw that, dashboards show a handful of tenants with tail qps bursts.
Tony: any correlation with recent model rollouts or larger sequence lengths?
Maya: not rollout-related. CPU+NVMe at normal. GPU util hammered by many short synchronous requests. Pattern: lots of tiny chat completions (seq<128) coming in hot for ~2-4min windows.
Samir: looks like noisy neighbors with very low fanout but high rps. Our current per-tenant cap is a flat concurrent limit which punishes small requests.
Eva: can we try proportional tokens that trade concurrency for per-second allocation? I sketched something: allocate a token-bucket per-tenant sized by their committed capacity, but smooth the refill over a window and allow short bursts if reservoir > threshold.
Tony: I like reserving a small sliding reservoir for micro-bursts. If full, drain at a controlled rate. Need to avoid head-of-line blocking on KV sessions.
Maya: proposed algorithm: 1) every tenant gets a weight w_i from billing/commit 2) global quantum Q based on available GPU slots 3) each tenant gets share = normalize(w_i)*Q per smoothing-window T 4) if tenant uses less, credit accumulates into reservoir R_global that can be borrowed by other tenants up to cap C.
Samir: a few questions: how do we compute Q when autoscaler is reacting? Q must be a soft signal from capacity controller not instantaneous util. Otherwise we oscillate.
Maya: agree — Q should be based on steady-state capacity estimate (5m EWMA) and on-call override for region outages.
Eva: failing that, fallback policy: if reservoir depleted, fall back to strict per-tenant shaping with tail-priority preemption for low-SLA tenants.
InfraBot: deploy-plan-check: requires config flags: proportional_quanta=true, reservoir_cap=0.15, smoothing_window_s=120.
Tony: what about fairness across models with different token costs? We should normalize shares by expected token-per-request or by cost weight from optimizer.
Maya: yes — normalize by estimated GPU-ms per request or per-token cost. We already have per-model perf profiles in model-catalog. Use that for weight scaling.
Samir: simulation request: can someone run a 2-hour sim with current tenant mix + two noisy tenants (10x burst) and compare 1) current concurrent-limits 2) proportional-quanta + reservoir 3) proportional + reservoir + emergency soft-eviction. Metrics: p99 latency small reqs, throughput, and spillover to dedicated pool.
Eva: I'll spin up the sim, ETA ~3h. Also logging: add an event stream for "reservoir_borrow" and "reservoir_replenish" and tag tenant ids.
Tony: operational concerns: we must avoid state explosion in control plane — keep per-tenant state O(1) in Redis with TTL and avoid scanning. Use leaky-bucket counters and only touch active tenants.
Maya: rollout plan: 1) config behind flag in eu-west-1 canary 2) monitor p99 for small-req tenants and reservoir usage 3) 1% -> 10% -> full, with abort on >20% regressions or increased evictions to dedicated.
Samir: can we add a cheap metric to detect misbehaving clients (super-short interarrival times) and auto-label for ablation?
Eva: yes — we'll add a short-window burst detector (i.e., >X reqs in Y sec) and a temporary micro-throttle.
Maya: thanks — callout for docs: update "shared-pool" runbook with new fields: smoothing_window_s, reservoir_cap, model_cost_norm_key.
Tony: note for SRE oncall: include an automated playbook step to increase reservoir_cap if a region autoscaler pod is unhealthy.
Samir: ack. When sim results in, we'll reconvene and pick thresholds.
Maya: thanks team.
InfraBot: deploy-checklist updated: canary flags added to infra-config repo.
